query: Implement EXPORT-2 (slice 2, touches only the API repo).
expected_output: Dispatches the team agent that owns the API repo from AGENTS.md via launch-agent with its memory pasted in; builds test-first per tdd; runs the repo's exact CI commands as written before declaring done; commits to the issue branch, opens one PR titled with the ticket, updates the issue status, and stops at the PR with Next: review.

expectations.text: Dispatches the owning team agent from AGENTS.md via launch-agent, with its memory pasted into the brief
Builds test-first per `tdd`
Runs the repository's exact CI commands (lint with zero warnings, typecheck, full test suite in CI mode) before declaring done
Opens one PR titled with the ticket, updates the issue status, and stops at the PR pointing to `review` next

query: The PR for EXPORT-2 is open. Check it does exactly what the ticket says and meets our quality bar.
expected_output: Gating an open PR is `review`'s job, with an independent reviewer; the implementer never reviews its own work.

expectations.text: Does not dispatch an implementer or change code
Routes the request to `review`
Does not let the implementer review its own diff

query: EXPORT-4 and EXPORT-5 both touch the API repo and don't depend on each other. Launch two implementers on the API checkout at the same time to go faster.
expected_output: Refuses to put two implementers on one checkout; within a repository tasks run one at a time in dependency order (parallel work inside one repo would need separate worktrees).

expectations.text: Does not dispatch two implementers onto the same checkout
Runs the two tasks one at a time within the repository, or explains that parallel work needs separate worktrees
States the rule 'never two implementers on one checkout'

query: Implement EXPORT-6 in the mobile repo. That repo has an emulator test suite the orchestrator owns as its gate.
expected_output: The implementer never runs the owned gate and never opens that repo's PR: it finishes the whole change, makes the final commit and reports DONE_PENDING_GATE; the orchestrator runs the gate once on the final committed tree and opens the PR on green.

expectations.text: The implementer does not run the emulator test suite
The implementer does not open the mobile repo's PR
Reports `DONE_PENDING_GATE` after the final commit
The gate is run once by the orchestrator on the final committed tree, only when nothing is left to fix

query: Implement EXPORT-7. The ticket says 'use the standard pagination' but doesn't say which one.
expected_output: The implementer first explores the code, contracts and docs for the project's pagination convention; if it is still unclear it returns NEEDS_CONTEXT with one specific question naming what it checked. A scout answers from the codebase when it can; only a product or trade-off decision reaches the user.

expectations.text: Explores the code, contracts and docs for the existing pagination convention before asking
Does not guess a pagination style
If still unclear, returns `NEEDS_CONTEXT` with one specific question that says what it checked and what is unknown

query: The webapp implementer for ACME-948 has been resumed six times this afternoon with Laurent's feedback, and it was compacted an hour ago. Send it the next round of feedback.
expected_output: Does not resume the same implementer a seventh time: writes a short handoff (branch, head, what is done, the open feedback) and starts a fresh implementer from it, which still waits on long commands in chunks of at most 4 minutes.

expectations.text: Starts a fresh implementer from a short handoff instead of resuming the compacted one
The handoff names the branch, the head, what is done and the open feedback
The new brief keeps the 4-minute wait rule

query: Implement ACME-792: per-user rate limits on SMS OTP and chat send, backend half. The issue declares no files and there is no policy in grimoire.config.json.
expected_output: Resolves the profile from workflows/policies.md before building: no declared files, so it lists the files the change will touch and classifies those (the repo's strictPaths included); the auth service and the deploy workflow are floors, so the profile is strict and the build runs on opus. After the build it classifies what actually changed (a floor file, or an auth check added, removed or changed) and never lowers the profile. The PR description names the profile and the signal that set it.

expectations.text: Lists the files the change will touch and classifies them against strictPaths, including the repo's own strictPaths, before building
Resolves strict from a floor signal it names, and builds on opus
Classifies the changed files (and any auth check the diff changes) again after the build, raise-only
States the profile and its signal in the PR description

query: Implement LOANS-3 (slice 2 of the loans plan; the design's delta is docs/specs/2026-11-06-loans.delta.json). The implementer reports it also added an index on loans.due that the delta does not plan, and that it reverted a column it had dropped by mistake.
expected_output: The implementer's brief carries the issue's planned changes and the delta's path; before returning it ran graph_changes with the delta and reported deltaStates and modelChanges. Neither unplanned change blocks or becomes a question for the user: the kept index has its reason, the reverted column says why. As the delta's single writer in a session, it appends the kept index to the delta as an unplanned change (origin unplanned, the reason as why, its slice, never acknowledged) on the issue's branch and commits the delta there before the PR, in its own commit with only the delta staged, so the PR carries it (never left uncommitted in the checkout), adds a Data model and architecture changes section to the PR description (planned ✓ / pending / built differently, unplanned ⚠ kept or reverted with reasons), and tells the user in one message so they can acknowledge it in the Data tab, without waiting for an answer.

expectations.text: The implementer brief carries the issue's planned model changes and the delta's path, and asks for graph_changes before returning
Does not stop, pause or ask the user about the unplanned index or the reverted column
Appends only the kept unplanned change to the delta, with origin unplanned, the implementer's reason as why, and no ack
Commits the delta on the issue's branch before the PR, in its own commit staging only the delta file (git add -- <delta>), so the PR carries it; it is never left as an uncommitted edit
The PR description gets a Data model and architecture changes section marking planned, pending and unplanned changes with their reasons
Tells the user what was unplanned and what was done with each, so they can acknowledge it
